research_question: Do local DINOv3 patch representations contain writer-specific information that transfers across Arabic and English handwriting?
supported_findings: Foreground DINOv3 patch tokens contain measurable cross-script writer information.
Same-writer local correspondence is above chance under the tested training-free matchers.
Mutual nearest-neighbor matching provides only modest standalone discrimination.
unsupported_findings: Local correspondence outperforms the global DINOv3 CLS baseline.
Local correspondence provides consistent complementary value beyond the global CLS score.
The exploration fusion gain generalizes consistently to writer-disjoint monitor writers.
decision: Do not proceed directly to a learnable StyleRouter or pair-conditioned partial-matching architecture from the current evidence.
interpretation: Training-free local correspondence shows transferable writer signal but does not provide robust additional verification value beyond the global DINOv3 representation. The feasibility result is mixed-to-negative for the proposed central method direction.
